extracted.intended_audience: General readers and researchers interested in U.S. elections, election results, and post‑election analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Post‑election summary and analysis of the 2024 United States presidential election, including state and county results, turnout, demographic swings, historical comparisons, media metrics, and expert commentary. Focus is on quantifying margins, swings, turnout patterns, demographic shifts, and post‑election effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: State margin-of-victory categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of states/districts by margin of victory (examples: Georgia 2.20%; New Hampshire 2.78%; Nevada 3.10%; categories include a 'between 5% and 10%' bracket listing Arizona 5.53%, Virginia 5.78%, New Jersey 5.91%, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to group jurisdictions by competitiveness (very close, close, moderately close). The article lists states and electoral votes falling into specific margin bands (e.g., between 5% and 10%) as examples of these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral votes per state/district
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of each state's (or congressional district's) electoral vote allocation alongside vote shares and margins (e.g., Georgia – 16 electoral votes; Arizona – 11 electoral votes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral vote totals are combined with margins to explain Electoral College outcomes and to compute overall Electoral College percentages (e.g., Trump won 58% of the Electoral College).

rubrics_metrics.name: County-level partisan extremes
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of counties (and equivalents) with the highest percentage voting for Democratic or Republican candidates (e.g., District of Columbia – 90.28% Democratic; Grant County, Nebraska – 95.90% Republican).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies geographic extremes to illustrate where each party's support is most concentrated; useful for highlighting polarization and strongholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps and cartograms (vote share, margin, county flips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple visualizations: results by vote share in each state, results by margin of victory, discontinuous cartograms scaled by Electoral College contribution, discretized hexagon cartograms, maps by county shaded by winner or vote share, county flips from 2020 to 2024, and congressional district results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual tools to communicate geographic distribution of support and relative weight of jurisdictions; cartograms emphasize Electoral College weight rather than geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swing (county-level change) and trend metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of swing in county margins from 2020 to 2024 and 'trend' which is swing relative to the national popular‑vote swing (e.g., almost all counties swung toward Trump; trend and swing maps shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify where and how vote margins shifted compared with prior elections; distinguishes absolute swing from relative trend versus national movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral College outcome contextualization (percentile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual metric: Trump's 58% Electoral College share places the win in approximately the 28th percentile of all presidential elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places the raw Electoral College result in historical perspective to gauge magnitude compared to prior elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular‑vote margin historical percentile
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical framing of popular‑vote margin: Trump's ~1.5% margin places his victory in the 20th percentile of presidential victory margins since 1828.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show how narrow or decisive a popular‑vote win is relative to historical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-level shifts relative to past elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of state shifts relative to 2020 and 2016 (e.g., no state shifted Democratic from 2020 to 2024; relative to 2016, 28 states shifted to the right with an average shift of ~1 point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies partisan movement over time at the state level to assess geographic directionality of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable historical firsts and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of historically notable outcomes (e.g., first president since Grover Cleveland in 1892 to win non‑consecutive terms; first time since 1892 the incumbent party lost in each of three consecutive presidential elections; first Republican to win Nevada since 2004; first election since 1976 where all 50 states + DC shifted toward same party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights unusual or precedent-setting features of the election to emphasize significance beyond raw numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic voting shifts and exit‑poll metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Exit‑poll and demographic findings (e.g., Harris won voters under 30 by 54–51% per exit polls; almost all demographic groups swung towards Trump from 2020 with exceptions; specifics on young men, minority groups, education and income groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to analyze which demographic cohorts shifted support and how that contributed to the overall result; includes subgroup percentages and noted exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnout composition and engagement metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of turnout and voter engagement: plurality of voters stayed home in 18 states; Catalist analysis showing Trump's victory rested on less engaged voters and weakened turnout among Democratic‑leaning groups; Pew analysis on electorate diversity and lower engagement compared with prior elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes not just turnout rate but the composition (new/infrequent voters vs. habitual voters) and how that affected partisan outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue salience and voter priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Polling and survey results on which issues drove votes (e.g., IMEU/YouGov finding for Biden‑2020 non‑Harris voters: Gaza 29%, economy 24%, Medicare/Social Security 12%, immigration 11%, healthcare 10%, abortion 9%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to explain voter decision drivers and why certain coalitions shifted; ranks issue importance for subgroups of voters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst and media explanatory frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative attributions from analysts and outlets (e.g., economy and inflation, immigration, anti‑incumbent environment, Biden association, messaging failures) explaining why Harris lost and Trump won.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides interpretive lenses — economic performance, messaging, candidate ties to incumbency — that analysts use to account for numerical results; not purely quantitative but essential to evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑election social and behavioral effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported social consequences after the result: spikes in crisis service usage for LGBTQ+ (Trevor Project, Crisis Text Line), 200× jump in inquiries to companies assisting wealthy Americans to secure foreign citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures downstream societal reactions and distress as immediate indicators of the election's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misinformation and denialism metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantified spread of 'stolen election' conspiracy claims (e.g., peak of 94,000 posts per hour on X; mentions like 'Trump cheated' receiving 92,100 mentions in a specified interval), and official refutations (CISA statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks scale and tempo of post‑election misinformation and platforms' amplification as a factor in the post‑election environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted harassment reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents of post‑election harassment: numerous Black Americans reported receiving threatening, racist text messages the day after the election; later similar reports by Latino and LGBTQIA students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents immediate harms and indicates targeted intimidation patterns following electoral outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media consumption and campaign outreach channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of media strategies and consumption: Trump's outreach via alternative media and influencers (Joe Rogan, Adin Ross, etc.); targeted advertising to individual undecided voters on streaming platforms vs. Harris' geography‑targeted ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses campaign effectiveness by channel choice and media consumption trends, including the role of influencers and targeted ads in reaching specific voter segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast and cable viewership metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewership numbers by network and time slot (e.g., 8:00–11:00 p.m. EST — Fox News 10,300,000; MSNBC 6,000,000; ABC 5,900,000; and cable totals across 6:00 p.m. to 3:00 a.m.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure audience size and distribution of election night coverage across networks and to infer where voters sought information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecasts and pre‑election ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to nonpartisan election forecasters (The Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball) and polling/forecast expectations (e.g., some forecasters stated before the election Biden would have been almost certain to lose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares pre‑election expectations to outcomes to evaluate forecasting performance and the reliability of predictive models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation with educational attainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that, among jurisdictions Harris won (19 states, DC, Nebraska's 2nd), all except New Mexico had above‑average educational attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights a demographic correlate (education level) associated with the geography of the vote; useful for demographic modeling and interpretation.
